title: Messi Back in Training at Inter Miami While Ronaldo Takes Extended Break From Al-Nassr
excerpt: The two football icons chart contrasting post-World Cup paths, with Messi returning to Inter Miami just 10 days after the final and Ronaldo given extended rest by Al-Nassr following Portugal's early exit.
body:
• Lionel Messi returned to Inter Miami training on July 29, just 10 days after Argentina's 1-0 World Cup final loss to Spain, and could feature in Leagues Cup matches starting August 5.
  • Cristiano Ronaldo remains on extended rest from Al-Nassr despite Portugal's earlier elimination in the round of 16 on July 6, with the club managing his workload ahead of the Saudi Pro League season.
  • Messi finished the 2026 World Cup with eight goals and four assists — career-highs at the tournament — while Ronaldo scored three goals but drew criticism for largely ineffective performances.
  • Both players are in the twilight of their careers, with the 39-year-old Messi and 41-year-old Ronaldo navigating very different club environments and competitive pressures.

Messi Wastes No Time Getting Back to Work

Lionel Messi touched down in Miami and reported to Inter Miami's Florida Blue Training Center on Wednesday, July 29, ending a brief vacation in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina. The 39-year-old had competed in every minute of Argentina's run to the 2026 World Cup final, where they fell 1-0 to Spain at MetLife Stadium on July 19 after a Ferran Torres goal in the 106th minute of extra time.

Despite the heartbreak, Messi chose not to take the full 21-day rest window mandated by FIFA and FIFPRO for post-tournament recovery. According to USA Today, he is not expected to feature in Saturday's MLS match against the Columbus Crew, but is likely to return for Inter Miami's Leagues Cup campaign, which begins August 5 against Atlético de San Luis.

"Messi delivered the most productive World Cup campaign of his career at 39 years old, bagging eight goals and four assists — both career-highs across his record-six World Cup appearances."

— Sports Illustrated

In Messi's absence, Inter Miami kept their season on track. Luis Suárez stepped up as the attacking focal point, helping the Herons secure victories over both Chicago Fire and CF Montréal. Head coach Guillermo Hoyos managed the squad effectively without his captain, but the return of Messi — and fellow Argentine Rodrigo De Paul — will be crucial as the defending Leagues Cup champions prepare to defend their title.

Ronaldo Given Extended Recovery Time

On the other side of the rivalry, Cristiano Ronaldo has taken a markedly different path. Portugal's World Cup campaign ended on July 6 with a 1-0 round-of-16 loss to Spain — the same opponent that beat Argentina in the final, but nearly two weeks earlier. Yet as of late July, Ronaldo had still not rejoined Al-Nassr for preseason preparations.

According to World Soccer Talk, the 41-year-old was absent from Al-Nassr's preseason friendly against Benfica B, with the club opting to manage his workload carefully ahead of another long Saudi Pro League season. Reports indicated Ronaldo was expected to begin a specialized conditioning program around July 27 under new manager Ange Postecoglou.

The cautious approach makes sense given the context. Ronaldo confirmed during the World Cup that it would be his final appearance at the tournament. He scored three goals — a brace against Uzbekistan that made him the first player to score in six World Cups, and a penalty against Croatia in the round of 32 — but his overall performances drew criticism. He managed just 25 touches in the opening 1-1 draw with DR Congo, his fewest in any major tournament match where he played the full 90 minutes, according to Opta.

Different Pressures, Different Timelines

The contrasting approaches reflect the different competitive environments each player operates in. Messi's Inter Miami are in the middle of an MLS season that runs through October, with the Leagues Cup adding further fixtures. Every week he misses puts the Herons at a disadvantage in a tight playoff race. The urgency is real.

Ronaldo faces no such pressure. The Saudi Pro League season does not resume for weeks, giving Al-Nassr the luxury of easing their star back into action. Having won the league title last season — Ronaldo's first domestic trophy with the club — the priority is keeping him fresh for a title defense rather than rushing him onto the pitch.

At 39 and 41 respectively, Messi and Ronaldo continue to defy the conventional career arc. Messi's eight World Cup goals this summer pushed him past records held by Just Fontaine and Jairzinho, while Ronaldo's three goals took his all-time World Cup tally to 10, surpassing Portugal legend Eusébio.

What Comes Next

For Messi, the immediate focus is the Leagues Cup and steering Inter Miami through the second half of the MLS season. For Ronaldo, preseason conditioning and a fresh start under Postecoglou await in Riyadh. Both men are running down the clock on extraordinary careers — but doing so at characteristically different speeds.
